chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Mansour ibn Hazim, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a house containing other houses, and their pathway was one shared in the courtyard of the house. So one of them sold his house to a man. Is it for his partners in the pathway that they can take the right of pre-emption? He said: If he sold the house and turned its door to a road other than that, then there is no pre-emption for them, and if he sold the pathway along with the house, then for them is the right of pre-emption.

key_terms.عَرْصَة: Courtyard or open space of a house

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for exercising the right of pre-emption (shuf'ah) in shared property according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the jurisprudential criteria for shuf'ah (pre-emption) in shared residential properties, emphasizing that the right depends on the continuity of access rather than mere ownership. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) distinguishes between selling the house with its original entrance versus relocating it, thereby protecting neighbors' interests in common courtyards (arshah). This ruling reflects the Shia emphasis on preserving communal harmony and preventing harm (darar) in urban living arrangements.
